name: Short Synthetic Straddle (Covered Ratio Write)
summary: 100 long shares plus two short ATM calls reproduces a short straddle at that strike; one call is covered by the shares and the second is naked, which is what makes it a Level 4 structure with unlimited upside risk.

legs.strike_rule: ATM: strike nearest spot, call delta 0.45-0.55. TWO contracts — the first covered by the shares, the SECOND UNCOVERED

max_profit: call_credit x 2 x 100 + (strike - entry_spot) x 100, realised if the underlying finishes exactly at the strike
max_loss: UNDEFINED (unlimited) above the strike — the second short call has no cover and loses 100 shares' worth per point above the breakeven

greeks.delta: ~0.00 at entry (+1.00 shares, -1.00 from two ATM calls)

breakevens: Upside: strike + (total_credit/100) + (strike - entry_spot)/100, approximately. Downside: entry_spot - total_credit/100.
when_to_use: Historically used by traders wanting short-vol exposure while holding shares. There is no use case on this account: the second call is naked. Included for completeness and as a pattern the classifier must recognise, especially because it can be created accidentally by selling a second covered call against the same 100 shares.
entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: the second short call is uncovered. Alpaca rejects a multi-leg order containing it, and rejects it as a standalone short call. Requires Level 4.
BLOCKED BY RISK POLICY even at Level 4: unbounded upside loss on a $50k account.

CLASSIFIER REQUIREMENT: check every cycle that (number of short calls x 100) <= shares held for every underlying. A covered-call program that sells a second contract against the same 100 shares creates exactly this structure without anyone deciding to.
Level-3-legal substitute: sell one covered call and buy a further OTM call to cap the second short — i.e. a covered call plus a call credit spread, which is fully defined-risk and Level 3 legal.
management_rules: If this exposure is ever detected, raise a critical alert and buy back the uncovered call immediately, or buy a protective further-OTM call to cap it in the same session.
No profit target or stop is specified because the position should not exist.
exit_rules: MANDATORY: close both short calls no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.

If spot > strike at any time on expiration day, close both short calls by 14:00 ET. Assignment on both delivers 200 shares — 100 held and 100 short — leaving a naked short share position over the weekend.
Close both short calls by 15:00 ET the session before any ex-dividend date if extrinsic < 1.25 x declared dividend; a ratio write on a dividend payer is an early-assignment magnet on both contracts.
If assigned on one or both, flatten the resulting share imbalance at the first available print.
assignment_risk: On both short calls, with only one of them covered. Assignment on both delivers 200 shares against 100 held, producing a naked short 100-share position. Partial assignment (one of two) is also possible and leaves an unbalanced, directional book. Dividend-driven early exercise applies to both contracts simultaneously.
buying_power: Shares at full cost or 50% Reg T, plus a full naked short call requirement for the second contract (roughly 20% of underlying value less OTM amount plus premium). About $7,000+ per unit on a $100 name.
common_mistakes: Creating it accidentally in a covered-call program by not reconciling short call count against share count. Believing the shares 'mostly' cover two calls.
zero_dte_notes: Never — unbounded risk plus certain assignment on at least one contract if the underlying closes above the strike.
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
